input.question: when you're sick, why do symptoms seem worse at night / when trying to sleep?
input.ground_truth: One of the mechanisms at work is the cortisol level. Cortisol is a steroid hormone your body produces, that (among very many other things) suppresses your immune system. But the Cortisol levels vary during the course of a day. As you might have guessed, the concentration of cortisol in your blood decreases during the day and reaches lower levels in the late evening and night. So basically your symptoms get worse, because there is less immunosuppressive Cortisol to fight the inflammation, which leads to more swelling and stronger pain signals being sent.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: when you're sick, why do symptoms seem worse at night / when trying to sleep?

Answer:

response.prediction: When you’re sick, your body is fighting germs. At night, you’re quiet and still, so you notice how you feel more. Also, when you lie down, mucus (the stuff that comes out of your nose) can build up and make you feel stuffy. Plus, your body’s temperature can go up a little at night, which can make you feel achy or uncomfortable. That’s why you might feel worse when you’re trying to sleep!
